rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent single mass in all four views, but it is closer to a generic stepped/extruded bar than to a neighborhood-living building with an active ground threshold and a legible public void. The sawtooth roof gives some section identity, yet the roof logic feels more like a repeated profile than a program-driven long-span or terrace/court relationship. The blue frontage edge is not convincingly answered by a public seam, undercut, or open ground; the mass remains largely sealed at the access side. Parcel containment appears intact, and the form is not visibly self-colliding across views, so the main issue is semantic: weak public-threshold response and only moderate program fit. Reference 1042657 is the closest transferable principle for stepped hierarchy; 1056601 and 1067792 support courtyard/edge mediation; 1042923 is counterfactual and only useful for a connective threshold idea.
